title: window.ml execution log export
description: One run's mechanics as a FILE, which is what the panel's download writes. A bare array was the obvious thing and is the wrong one: it carries no version, nothing saying which run it is of, and nothing saying when it was taken — all three of which a file read six months later needs and a panel does not. Normative shape, published as `docs/spec/run-log.schema.json` (generated from here; see scripts/gen-export-schema.mjs).

run.description: The run it is of — absent when the whole ring was exported rather than one run's records.

RunLogEvent.description: One thing the machinery did on a run's behalf. A housekeeping event plus WHOSE run it was, since the whole point is reading one run's mechanics beside its steps. `subsystem` and `kind` are open by intent, exactly as they are there: a new mechanism adds its own rather than extending an enum every consumer generated from.

level.description: `"warn"` when something went wrong and was worked around, `"error"` when it was not. Absent means `"info"`.

reason.description: Why: `"budget"`, `"idle"`, `"timeout"`, `"session-end"`, … — what tells a budget eviction from an idle one.

key.description: What it acted on: a URL, a pointer id, a session hash. Withheld from a page reading events it did not report.

tab.description: The reporting tab, for `origin: "page"` — how a page's own events are told from another tab's.

run.description: The run's id, which is its session hash (`runId: runHash`, ml-agent-run.ts).

detail.description: Anything else: flat, as in the housekeeping log, except on `cell`/`facts` (CellFactsDetail).

CellFactsDetail.description: The ONE nested `detail`: subsystem `cell`, kind `facts` (docs/spec/CELL_FACTS.md, Half 1). `seq` is the step it describes; `cell` is what sanitizeCellFacts returned. Validated by enumeration, never passed through.

CellFacts.description: What a cell did, as the export and the execution log carry it. Every field but `lang` and `ran` may be absent.

realm.description: JS only: where its dialect evaluator ran.

class.description: Python only: the ladder's class of the worker when the cell started (ruling 102); absent for `not-run`.

why.description: For `outside` and `not-run`: why it was not inside. `name` is the first refused name, an identifier.

steps.description: JS only: the step meter at the cell's end, for an inside cell and for one that tripped the budget.

lifted.description: JS inside cells: the host functions called, largest charge first.

liftedMore.description: Rows of `lifted` cut by the row cap or the size bound.

wire.description: JS inside cells and every Python cell: the `ml` members called over the wire.

wireMore.description: Rows of `wire` cut by the row cap or the size bound.

marked.description: Python: this cell set the outside mark on its worker.

CellLifted.description: One lifted or host function the cell called, and the steps charged for it (its callbacks' steps are the cell's own).

CellWire.description: One `ml` wire member the cell called.
